method: v2 baseline + audit-driven gap fills (thermoelectric, optical metrology, implant bioelectronics sharpening, computer architecture) + explicit out_of_scope routing and strengthened tie-breaks

themes.name: AI/ML, Supercomputing & Quantum Computing
themes.scope_note: This theme encompasses foundational and applied research in artificial intelligence, machine learning, high-performance computing, and quantum computing. Core domains include machine learning algorithms and neural network architectures (from feature selection to deep learning), natural language processing and information retrieval systems (text analysis, entity resolution, summarization), theoretical computer science (algorithm design, complexity analysis, graph and parallel algorithms), and mathematical foundations for dynamical systems (control theory, Lyapunov stability, system identification). Also included are computational methods for solving differential equations and simulating complex physical phenomena, particularly in fluid mechanics and flow analysis. Papers in this theme typically present advances in learning algorithms, algorithmic techniques, NLP methods, or mathematical frameworks for analyzing dynamical systems—such as novel neural network architectures for color quantization, VC dimension bounds, latent Dirichlet allocation for selectional preferences, Lyapunov function computation, or numerical schemes for compressible flows. Explicitly excluded are: quantum devices, quantum materials, and semiconductor fabrication (assign to Quantum Technologies & Semiconductor Technology); biomaterial synthesis and characterization not tied to a specific clinical application (assign to Advanced Materials & Devices); and wireless communication systems, signal modulation, and electromagnetic wave propagation (assign to Next-Gen Communication). When a paper addresses quantum algorithms, quantum information theory, or quantum computing as a computational paradigm, it belongs in this theme; conversely, quantum photonic devices and quantum material systems belong in Quantum Technologies. When applying machine learning methods to a clinical problem, classify by the primary contribution: if the advance is in the learning algorithm itself, assign to this theme; if the advance is in medical imaging, diagnostics, or clinical application, assign to Healthcare & MedTech.  Computer architecture and systems (VLIW, interconnects, microarchitecture) belong here under Computer Architecture & Systems.

themes.name: Advanced Materials & Devices
themes.scope_note: Advanced Materials & Devices encompasses the discovery, synthesis, characterization, and fundamental property engineering of new and engineered materials across polymers, metals, ceramics, composites, and nanomaterials, spanning from bio-based polymers and sustainable synthesis methods to ferroelectric ceramics, rare-earth phosphors, and thin-film nanostructures. This theme covers microstructural analysis, structure-property relationships, mechanical and thermal behavior, optical and magnetic properties, and materials design—including examples such as green synthesis of bio-based nanoparticles, grain boundary behavior in metallic alloys, ion-beam modification of thin films, dielectric properties of ceramic composites, and polymer nanocomposite characterization via spectroscopy. Materials processing and joining techniques (machining, welding, additive manufacturing) belong instead to Manufacturing & Industry 4.0, while materials engineered for specific clinical or therapeutic applications (drug delivery vehicles, tissue scaffolds, diagnostic biosensors) go to Healthcare & MedTech. Biomaterials designed for general use without a targeted therapeutic application—such as cellulose-based foams or chitosan nanoparticles for adsorption or multifunctional characteristics—remain in Advanced Materials & Devices. If a paper's primary contribution is a quantum device, semiconductor fabrication process, or photodetection system, assign it to Quantum Technologies & Semiconductor Technology; if the contribution is quantum algorithms or quantum information science, assign it to AI/ML, Supercomputing & Quantum Computing. Energy-storage or energy-conversion materials (batteries, photovoltaic absorbers, thermoelectric materials) belong to Energy, Sustainability & Climate Change rather than this theme. Functional/antibacterial/antimicrobial nanomaterials and nanoparticle materials studied for their material properties—even when an antibacterial, antimicrobial, or other biological assay is used to characterize the material—belong in Advanced Materials & Devices (e.g., Bio-based Materials & Polymers or the relevant materials domain), NOT in Healthcare's clinical domains. Tie-break: antibacterial/antimicrobial or bioactivity testing of a material, where the contribution is the material itself, → Advanced Materials; only assign Healthcare when there is a specific clinical/therapeutic use in patients.

themes.name: Energy, Sustainability & Climate Change
themes.scope_note: This theme encompasses research on energy generation, conversion, storage, and distribution technologies; sustainability assessment and natural resource management; and climate dynamics and regional modeling relevant to India's energy transition and environmental challenges. Core domains include biomass and biofuel conversion from agricultural residues, solar thermal and photovoltaic energy systems, grid integration and smart microgrids for renewable energy, carbon utilization and catalytic conversion of CO₂ and biomass, environmental assessment and land-use management, monsoon dynamics and regional climate modeling, and electric vehicle battery and charging systems. Research on the physics, chemistry, and engineering of energy materials and devices belongs here—such as perovskite solar cells, iron-cerium catalysts for hydrogen production, or battery management systems—whereas foundational discovery, synthesis, and characterization of novel materials without a specific energy application goes to Advanced Materials & Devices. Energy-efficient building design, urban energy systems, and smart grid infrastructure as critical infrastructure belong to Smart & Sustainable Infrastructure, not here. Machine learning applications to energy systems or climate modeling belong in AI/ML, Supercomputing & Quantum Computing if the methodological contribution (algorithm, model architecture) is the primary focus; conversely, if a paper develops a neural network model specifically to predict solar thermal performance or grid control, it is assigned here because the energy engineering problem is primary. Papers on agricultural sustainability, soil health, ecosystem services, and environmental remediation are included when linked to energy, land use, or climate; general soil mechanics or wastewater treatment as infrastructure belongs to Smart & Sustainable Infrastructure. Climate simulation, monsoon dynamics, and atmospheric modeling using regional climate models and satellite data are central to this theme, whereas broader atmospheric physics or plasma-electromagnetic phenomena unrelated to climate belong elsewhere.  Thermoelectric and solid-state energy-harvesting MATERIALS are in-theme under Thermoelectric & Energy-Harvesting Materials.

themes.name: Healthcare & MedTech
themes.scope_note: Healthcare & MedTech encompasses the design, development, and clinical application of therapeutic agents, medical devices, diagnostic systems, and regenerative constructs aimed at disease prevention, detection, and treatment in human health. This includes drug delivery systems and molecular therapeutics (e.g., engineered nanoparticles with platinum cargo for cancer treatment), clinical AI and medical imaging analytics for diagnosis and decision support, tissue engineering and biomaterial scaffolds for wound healing and organ repair, biomechanical analysis of human tissues and musculoskeletal systems, biomarkers and point-of-care diagnostics, cellular and molecular investigations of disease mechanisms, biosensors for clinical monitoring, infectious disease pathogenesis, biopharmaceutical manufacturing and quality control, and neuroscience research on neural signaling and neurological conditions. When a biomaterial or scaffold is designed and characterized specifically for a clinical or therapeutic application (e.g., agar-gelatin scaffolds for tissue engineering, composite scaffolds for hemostasis), it belongs in Healthcare & MedTech; discovery and synthesis of general-purpose biomaterials without explicit therapeutic intent belong in Advanced Materials & Devices instead. When machine learning or AI methods are applied to medical imaging, clinical decision-making, or disease prediction in a healthcare context, the work belongs here; if the primary contribution is a novel ML algorithm or computational method independent of healthcare application, it belongs in AI/ML, Supercomputing & Quantum Computing instead. Wearable sensors and biosensors developed for clinical monitoring (e.g., wrap-around coils for joint flexion monitoring) are included here, whereas general sensor device physics or semiconductor fabrication belongs in Quantum Technologies & Semiconductor Technology. Biomanufacturing and fermentation processes directed toward biopharmaceutical production belong here, while general fermentation and bioprocess engineering belong in Manufacturing & Industry 4.0.  Implant wireless power and IMD bioelectronics interfaces belong under Clinical Biosensors & Implant Bioelectronics. Downstream biopharma PAT/QC belongs under Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing & Quality.

themes.name: Manufacturing & Industry 4.0
themes.scope_note: Manufacturing & Industry 4.0 encompasses the design, control, optimization, and characterization of industrial production processes and equipment, spanning electrical drives and power conversion, rotating machinery dynamics, precision machining and material joining, surface finishing, multiphase flow systems, and biomanufacturing. The theme covers experimental and computational studies of friction, wear, lubrication, vibration analysis, material mechanical behavior under manufacturing conditions, textile production, and fermentation scaling—as exemplified by research on harmonic mitigation in motor drives, bearing performance with nano-lubricants, hot embossing for microstructures, ultrasonic welding of dissimilar joints, yarn and fabric characterization, rotor dynamics diagnosis, and particle-laden flow manipulation. Explicitly excluded: discovery, synthesis, or fundamental characterization of new materials not tied to a specific manufacturing process belongs to Advanced Materials & Devices; energy generation, storage, or conversion technologies belong to Energy, Sustainability & Climate Change, while energy-efficient buildings and smart grids as infrastructure belong to Smart & Sustainable Infrastructure; CFD as a general computational method for non-manufacturing applications belongs to AI/ML, Supercomputing & Quantum Computing; and control systems theory in isolation belongs to AI/ML. Tie-break rule: if a paper's primary contribution is a processing or joining technique applied to materials, or characterization of material behavior during manufacturing, assign it here; if the primary contribution is synthesis or discovery of a new material or material class itself, assign it to Advanced Materials & Devices. Similarly, if research on bearings, shafts, or rotating equipment focuses on production, assembly, or operational diagnostics in industrial context, it belongs here; if it is fundamental materials science of bearing alloys, assign to Advanced Materials & Devices.

themes.name: Next-Gen Communication
themes.scope_note: Next-Gen Communication encompasses the physical layer, signal processing, and network architecture of wireless and optical communication systems. This includes antenna and RF design for microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies; signal modulation, detection, and equalization techniques; beamforming and direction-of-arrival estimation using array signal processing; cooperative and relay-based multi-hop networks; free-space optical links addressing fading and atmospheric effects; microwave photonic subsystems for RF signal processing; MAC protocols and resource allocation in wireless networks; and nonlinear electromagnetic-plasma interactions for wave and wakefield generation. Papers addressing the design of beamforming algorithms, performance analysis of relay networks, atmospheric turbulence mitigation in FSO systems, Brillouin-based photonic filters, QPSK detection schemes, channel access delay modeling, and plasma-wave physics all belong here. Excluded are: machine learning methods for communication (route to AI/ML, Supercomputing & Quantum Computing); quantum algorithms and quantum information processing (route to AI/ML); quantum photonic devices and semiconductor fabrication (route to Quantum Technologies & Semiconductor Technology); and general information management or telecommunications policy (route to Social Sciences, Humanities & Management). If a paper's primary contribution is a learning algorithm or AI method applied to communication, assign it to AI/ML; if it concerns quantum devices, quantum materials, or semiconductor physics, assign it to Quantum Technologies. Plasma-wave and electromagnetic-plasma physics remains in Next-Gen Communication.

themes.name: Quantum Technologies & Semiconductor Technology
themes.scope_note: This theme encompasses the design, fabrication, characterization, and device physics of quantum and semiconductor technologies, spanning from ultrascale analog circuit design in nanoscale CMOS to advanced photonic and spintronic devices. Core research includes ultra-low voltage analog integrated circuits, semiconductor photovoltaic and photodetection devices, resistive memory and neuromorphic computing hardware, quantum light generation and integrated quantum photonic processors, structured light and polarization engineering, spintronics and magnetic devices, fiber photonic systems, wide bandgap semiconductors, and plasmonic and fiber optic sensors. The theme focuses on the physical mechanisms, device-level implementations, fabrication techniques, and experimental characterization of these technologies—for example, papers on photon pair sources, magnetic tunnel junctions, RRAM-based stochastic neurons, or polarization singularity generation all belong here. Excluded from this theme are quantum algorithms, quantum information theory, and quantum computing as computation models, which belong to AI/ML, Supercomputing & Quantum Computing; general material discovery and synthesis that is not tied to a specific device or technology demonstration, which belongs to Advanced Materials & Devices; and energy generation or storage systems intended primarily for grid integration or infrastructure applications, which belong to Energy, Sustainability & Climate Change. When a paper involves quantum materials or devices (e.g., photon sources, entanglement generation, quantum memory), assign it here; when it involves quantum algorithms or information-theoretic methods for computation, assign it to the AI/ML theme. When a paper combines semiconductor physics with energy conversion (e.g., photovoltaic cell design or characterization), assign it to this theme; only advanced grid-integrated solar systems or large-scale energy infrastructure applications go to the Energy theme.  Optical/interferometric metrology instrumentation belongs here under Optical Metrology & Interferometric Instrumentation.

themes.name: Smart & Sustainable Infrastructure
themes.scope_note: Smart & Sustainable Infrastructure encompasses the design, modeling, analysis, and optimization of engineered systems that support urban and regional development while minimizing environmental impact. The theme covers power systems and smart grids; geotechnical and structural engineering for foundations and dynamic systems; transportation networks and traffic management; water resources, hydrology, and wastewater treatment; building energy performance and thermal design; urban air quality monitoring; and seismic resilience of infrastructure. Papers in this theme typically address infrastructure performance, resilience, efficiency, and environmental quality at the systems or asset level—such as load flow analysis in grids, soil reinforcement behavior, traffic flow prediction, water quality simulation in rivers, thermal retrofit of buildings, or air pollutant modeling in cities. Excluded from this theme are energy generation, storage, and conversion technologies (e.g., photovoltaic materials, battery systems, biomass conversion), which belong in Energy, Sustainability & Climate Change; materials discovery and synthesis, which belong in Advanced Materials & Devices; AI/ML methods developed primarily as algorithmic contributions, which belong in AI/ML, Supercomputing & Quantum Computing; and policy, economics, or social aspects of infrastructure, which belong in Social Sciences, Humanities & Management. When a paper applies machine learning or computational methods to infrastructure problems (e.g., kriging for traffic speed estimation, machine learning for air pollutant factor analysis), assign it to Smart & Sustainable Infrastructure if the focus is on the infrastructure application and outcomes; assign it to AI/ML only if the contribution is methodological advancement in the algorithm itself. When a paper addresses energy efficiency in buildings or smart grid operations as infrastructure systems, it belongs in Smart & Sustainable Infrastructure; only assign to Energy theme if it concerns primary energy generation or storage technologies.

themes.name: Social Sciences, Humanities & Management
themes.scope_note: This theme encompasses research in economics, management science, information systems, library science, humanities, and cultural studies—focusing on organizational behavior, institutional practice, human experience, and social outcomes rather than technological innovation per se. Included domains span digital transformation adoption in enterprises and government, information management as professional practice, supply chain and operations management, development economics and poverty analysis, ethnographic studies of religion and identity, international business strategy, agricultural and consumer economics, digital culture and user experience, computational linguistics applied to language analysis, and social media analytics. Research on economic development and welfare schemes, caste and inequality in social programs, border studies and religious conversion, cross-border acquisitions and firm strategy, library digitization projects, and supply chain coordination all exemplify the scope. Excluded: machine learning and NLP algorithms developed primarily as computational methods (go to AI/ML theme); biomaterials designed for clinical therapeutic application (go to Healthcare & MedTech); energy generation and storage technologies (go to Energy theme); and general material synthesis and characterization (go to Advanced Materials). Tie-break rule for NLP: if the primary contribution is a computational linguistics method or parsing algorithm for processing Indian or classical languages, assign to this theme's Computational Linguistics domain; if the contribution is a machine learning algorithm whose application happens to be language, assign to AI/ML. Tie-break rule for digital systems: information systems and e-governance as organizational adoption and managerial practice belong here; the underlying AI/ML methods or infrastructure systems belong in their respective themes. Tie-break rule for economics and policy: empirical analysis of welfare schemes, development outcomes, agricultural value chains, and behavioral consumer research belong here; the statistical or experimental methodology used is secondary to the social/economic subject matter.

global_rules: OUT-OF-SCOPE: particle-accelerator RF / LLRF / cavity phase-locking / superconducting-accelerator instrumentation with no applied power-grid, communications, or manufacturing target → unclassifiable=true with reason starting 'out_of_scope: accelerator RF instrumentation'.

OUT-OF-SCOPE / EDGE: automotive fuel-additive screening for engine-deposit control with no materials-process or manufacturing contribution → unclassifiable=true with reason 'out_of_scope: fuel-additive engine-deposit screening' (do NOT force into Materials, Joining & Mechanical Behavior).

TIE-BREAK: downstream biopharma PAT / mAb / biosimilar quality, aggregation, glycosylation, 2D-LC characterization → Healthcare / Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing & Quality (NOT Manufacturing / Biomanufacturing & Fermentation).

TIE-BREAK: mechanism-design / peer-prediction / algorithmic game-theory / incentive-compatible algorithms → AI/ML / Algorithms & Computational Complexity (NOT Social Sciences / Digital Culture & Consumer Experience).
TIE-BREAK: thermoelectric / Seebeck / waste-heat-to-electricity MATERIALS → Energy / Thermoelectric & Energy-Harvesting Materials (NOT Energy Storage Materials; NOT Solar Thermal).

TIE-BREAK: optical / interferometric metrology instrumentation (white-light interferometry, interferometric microscopes, displacement metrology) → Quantum / Optical Metrology & Interferometric Instrumentation (NOT Fiber Photonic Devices unless the contribution is a fiber component).

TIE-BREAK: implantable medical device (IMD) wireless power transfer / inductive / magnetic coupling hardware for implants → Healthcare / Clinical Biosensors & Implant Bioelectronics (NOT general power electronics).

TIE-BREAK: computer architecture / VLIW / interconnect / microarchitecture / memory hierarchy / ISA → AI/ML / Computer Architecture & Systems (NOT Algorithms & Computational Complexity unless the novelty is pure algorithms).
